next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 General Election

glance_notes.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Georgia's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5, 2026.

glance_notes.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — How-to Guide: Voting
glance_notes.text: Three Weeks of Early Voting: Georgia provides three weeks of in-person early voting before the General Election, including two Saturdays. Counties may also offer Sunday voting.

glance_notes.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 General Election
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any registered Georgia voter may request an absentee ballot for an election without needing to provide an excuse for being absent on Election Day.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Georgia residents can register online through the Georgia Secretary of State, submit a paper application, or register through participating government agencies. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be a legal resident of Georgia and the county where you register, and be at least 17 1/2 years old. You must be at least 18 to vote. You cannot register while serving a sentence imposed for a felony conviction or if you have been judicially determined to be mentally incompetent.
register.glance_value: Register online, by paper or through an agency
register.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — How-to Guide: Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Additional verification source: Georgia Secretary of State Elections FAQ — [https://sos.ga.gov/page/elections-faq](https://sos.ga.gov/page/elections-faq) — directly establishes citizenship, Georgia and county residence, age, felony-sentence and mental-competency eligibility requirements. Georgia Secretary of State Voter Resources — [https://sos.ga.gov/voter-resources](https://sos.ga.gov/voter-resources) — confirms online, paper and government-agency registration methods.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Georgia's My Voter Page to check your voter registration status and review the registration information your county has on file. My Voter Page also provides your Election Day polling place, early-voting locations, absentee application and ballot status, sample ballot, elected officials and provisional-ballot status. Your county voter registration office retains the official registration record.
check_registration.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — My Voter Page
check_registration.internal_note: Additional verification source: Georgia Secretary of State How-to Guide: Register to Vote — [https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-register-vote](https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-register-vote) — lists the information available through MVP. How-to Guide: Voting — [https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-voting](https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-voting) — clarifies that MVP displays data extracted from the statewide database but the county voter registration office retains the official registration record.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Georgia's regular voter registration deadline is the fifth Monday before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline to register or change your address is October 5, 2026. A mailed voter registration application must be postmarked by the applicable registration deadline.
deadlines.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Calendar directly establishes October 5 as the General Election registration and address-change deadline, citing O.C.G.A. §§ 21-2-224(a) and 21-2-218. Additional verification source: Georgia Secretary of State Voter Registration Drive — [https://sos.ga.gov/page/voter-registration-drive](https://sos.ga.gov/page/voter-registration-drive) — establishes the fifth-Monday rule and states that mailed applications must be postmarked by the deadline.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: On Election Day, Georgia voters vote at the polling place assigned to their precinct. Use My Voter Page to find your assigned Election Day polling place. Early voting works differently: during the early-voting period, you may vote at any early-voting location within your county.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned precinct with MVP
polling_place.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — My Voter Page
polling_place.internal_note: Additional verification source: Georgia Secretary of State How-to Guide: Voting — [https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-voting](https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-voting) — establishes assigned Election Day polling-place voting and countywide early-voting-site use. Georgia Secretary of State Elections FAQ — [https://sos.ga.gov/page/elections-faq](https://sos.ga.gov/page/elections-faq) — also directs voters to MVP for both locations.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Georgia voters may vote in person at their assigned polling place on Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, polls are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. If you are in line by 7:00 p.m., you are allowed to vote. Georgia requires an acceptable government-issued photo ID for in-person voting. A voter whose eligibility cannot be determined at the polling place may be entitled to cast a provisional ballot.
election_day.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — How-to Guide: Voting
election_day.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes Election Day voting at the assigned polling place, 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. hours, protection for voters in line at 7:00 p.m., photo-ID requirement and provisional voting. Election-specific verification: Georgia Secretary of State 2026 Election Calendar — [https://sos.ga.gov/sites/default/files/forms/2026%20Elections%20Calendar_0.pdf](https://sos.ga.gov/sites/default/files/forms/2026%20Elections%20Calendar_0.pdf) — confirms November 3 and the same polling hours.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Georgia polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line by 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Calendar directly states that polls for the November 3 General Election are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., citing O.C.G.A. § 21-2-403. Additional verification source for the in-line-at-closing rule: [https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-voting](https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-voting).

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Georgia provides in-person early voting before the General Election. Voters have three weeks of early voting, including two Saturdays, and counties may also offer Sunday voting. During early voting, you may vote at any early-voting location in your county rather than being limited to your assigned Election Day precinct. Locations and daily hours are set locally, so use My Voter Page to find your county's current early-voting sites and schedules.
early_voting.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — How-to Guide: Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes three weeks of early voting, two Saturdays, optional Sunday voting and countywide early-voting-site use. The November 3, 2026 General Election page — [https://sos.ga.gov/november-3-2026-general-election](https://sos.ga.gov/november-3-2026-general-election) — repeats these rules and directs voters to county-specific locations and hours. Because exact locations, Sunday availability and daily schedules are county-specific, no unsupported statewide daily schedule is stated.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Georgia voter may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee-ballot requests became available August 17, and the deadline for the county to receive an ordinary absentee-ballot application is October 23, 2026, 11 days before Election Day. Counties begin mailing non-UOCAVA absentee ballots October 5. A completed ordinary absentee ballot must reach the county election office by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day to be counted. Georgia permits absentee ballots to be returned by mail and through authorized ballot drop boxes during the period and hours allowed by state law.
absentee_mail.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 General Election
absentee_mail.internal_note: Primary election page confirms no-excuse absentee voting and that requests for the November election became available August 17. Official absentee application — [https://sos.ga.gov/absenteeballotapplication20212](https://sos.ga.gov/absenteeballotapplication20212) — states applications must be received 11 days before the election. Official 2026 Election Calendar — [https://sos.ga.gov/2026-elections-calendar](https://sos.ga.gov/2026-elections-calendar) — establishes October 5 as the first day to mail non-UOCAVA absentee ballots. Georgia law requires ordinary absentee ballots to be received by close of polls; UOCAVA ballots have a separate three-business-day receipt rule documented in military_overseas. Current law also limits hand delivery and drop-box availability, so voters should follow county instructions rather than assuming a drop box is available through Election Day.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Georgia requires photo identification for in-person voting. Acceptable identification includes a valid state or federal government-issued photo ID, including a free Georgia voter ID card; a Georgia driver's license even if expired; a student photo ID from a Georgia public college or university; a valid government employee photo ID; a valid U.S. passport; a valid U.S. military photo ID; or a valid tribal photo ID. Voters who do not have an acceptable photo ID can obtain a free identification card through a county registrar's office or the Georgia Department of Driver Services. Georgia also requires identifying information or documentation when requesting an absentee ballot, but those absentee requirements are different from the identification shown when voting in person.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID required for in-person voting
voter_id.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — Georgia Voter Identification Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: Primary source directly lists the seven categories of acceptable in-person photo identification, confirms a Georgia driver's license may be expired, and explains free voter ID availability. The same official source separately describes identification requirements for absentee voting. Registration identification, in-person voting identification and absentee application identification are intentionally not conflated.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Georgia law requires counties to provide polling places accessible to voters with disabilities. Georgia's voting system includes accessibility features such as audio ballots through a headset, large controls for voters with limited mobility and compatibility with sip-and-puff devices. Voters who need assistance may receive help as allowed by law. A voter who is age 75 or older, or who has a disability and requires assistance in voting, may vote at the next available voting booth without waiting in line.
accessible_voting.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — Elections FAQ
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State FAQ directly establishes accessible polling-place requirements, audio/headset voting, large controls, sip-and-puff compatibility and the line-access provision for voters age 75 or older or voters with disabilities requiring assistance, citing O.C.G.A. § 21-2-409. Georgia Voter Resources — [https://sos.ga.gov/voter-resources](https://sos.ga.gov/voter-resources) — independently directs voters to disability voting assistance resources.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Georgia provides special voting procedures for voters covered by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act, including qualifying military members, eligible family members and U.S. citizens living abroad. These voters can use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request absentee ballots and may receive ballots electronically for federal elections or by mail. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as an emergency backup when a properly requested ballot does not arrive. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, an eligible UOCAVA ballot postmarked by Election Day can be counted if the county receives it by November 6, 2026.
military_overseas.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: Primary source establishes UOCAVA coverage, FPCA use, electronic or mail ballot delivery, FWAB availability and the rule that ballots postmarked by Election Day are counted if received within three days. Election-specific verification: Georgia Secretary of State 2026 Election Calendar — [https://sos.ga.gov/sites/default/files/forms/2026%20Elections%20Calendar_0.pdf](https://sos.ga.gov/sites/default/files/forms/2026%20Elections%20Calendar_0.pdf) — establishes November 6, 2026 as the UOCAVA ballot receipt deadline and describes it as three business days following the election. Returned voted ballots are not accepted by fax or email.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Georgia when they are domiciled in Georgia and otherwise meet the state's voter eligibility requirements. Georgia law authorizes presidents of public and private colleges and universities in the state, or their properly designated representatives, to register qualified students who are domiciled in Georgia. A student voting in person may use a student photo identification card issued by a Georgia public college or university as an acceptable form of voter identification.
student_voting.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — Election Rules, Subject 183-1-6
student_voting.internal_note: Georgia Election Rule 183-1-6-.05 directly establishes voter-registration authority for qualified students domiciled in Georgia. General eligibility requirements are established by Georgia Secretary of State Elections FAQ — [https://sos.ga.gov/page/elections-faq](https://sos.ga.gov/page/elections-faq). Student ID acceptance is established by Georgia Voter Identification Requirements — [https://sos.ga.gov/page/georgia-voter-identification-requirements](https://sos.ga.gov/page/georgia-voter-identification-requirements). The official sources reviewed do not establish that attending college in Georgia alone creates Georgia domicile, so no such claim is made.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Georgia voters can view their official sample ballot through My Voter Page when the ballot for an upcoming election is available. The sample ballot reflects the contests and ballot questions associated with the voter's registration and districts. A sample ballot is for information and planning only and cannot be returned as an official ballot.
sample_ballot.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — My Voter Page
sample_ballot.internal_note: Georgia Secretary of State How-to Guide: Register to Vote — [https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-register-vote](https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/how-guide-register-vote) — identifies the sample ballot for the upcoming election as an MVP feature. Additional official source: [https://sos.ga.gov/news/raffensperger-sample-ballots-now-available-my-voter-page](https://sos.ga.gov/news/raffensperger-sample-ballots-now-available-my-voter-page) — explains that MVP sample ballots reflect the voter's ballot and cannot be used as an official ballot. The November 3, 2026 General Election page also identifies MVP as the voter portal.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Georgia Secretary of State, Elections Division, 2 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive SE, Suite 802, Floyd West Tower, Atlanta, GA 30334. Phone: 404-656-2871. For questions about your individual voter registration, absentee ballot, polling place or county election administration, contact your county election office.
contact.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: The current November 3, 2026 General Election page directly verifies the Elections Division address and 404-656-2871 phone number. Georgia Voter Resources — [https://sos.ga.gov/voter-resources](https://sos.ga.gov/voter-resources) — establishes that local county officials run elections and county registrars determine voter eligibility. The live Secretary of State pages expose the Elections Division email only through a protected 'Send Email' control rather than as directly readable text, so no unverified email address is placed in reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Georgia Secretary of State Elections website for statewide voting information and My Voter Page for registration status, polling locations, early-voting locations, absentee-ballot status and sample ballots. Georgia elections are administered locally by county election offices, and county registrars determine voter eligibility. Contact your county election office for local voting sites, county-specific schedules and individual registration or ballot questions.
